facts.text: The Victorian Arcade, once called the Digbeth Arcade, opened its doors in 1897, adding a splash of late‑Victorian charm to Walsall’s town centre.
Queen Mary's Grammar School, founded in 1554, still wears the Tudor Rose and a sheaf of arrows as its emblem, a nod to the queen’s own heritage.
Walsall’s first cinema began showing films in 1908, but post‑war television boom eventually led to the closure of all local theatres.
Barr Beacon rises to the highest point eastward from the UK’s mainland until the Ural Mountains, making it a unique geographic landmark in Walsall.
Matthew’s Church, originally dedicated to All Saints, still houses a 13th‑century inner crypt that survived the town’s many redevelopment waves.
In 1966, Walsall expanded its boundaries to include most of Darlaston and Willenhall, then later joined the newly formed West Midlands county.
